concepts.name: Intuitive limit of a function
concepts.summary: Explain that a limit describes the value a function approaches as the input nears a point, regardless of the value at that point.

concepts.name: One-sided limits
concepts.summary: Distinguish left and right approach and state that a two-sided limit exists only when both agree.

concepts.name: Continuity at a point
concepts.summary: State the three conditions for continuity (defined, limit exists, equal) and recognise breaks in a graph.

concepts.name: Average rate of change
concepts.summary: Interpret the slope of a secant line as average rate of change over an interval.

concepts.name: Instantaneous rate and tangent
concepts.summary: Describe the derivative as the slope of the tangent line, obtained as secant slopes approach a limit.

concepts.name: Derivative notation
concepts.summary: Recognise and read f'(x), dy/dx and d/dx as notations for the derivative.

misconceptions.text: The limit of a function at a point is always just the function's value at that point.
If a limit exists at a point, the function must be defined there.
The derivative is the slope between two separate points on the graph, not a limiting value.

concepts.name: Evaluating limits algebraically
concepts.summary: Compute limits using limit laws, substitution, factoring, and conjugates to remove indeterminate 0/0 forms.

concepts.name: Limits at infinity
concepts.summary: Find limits as x grows without bound and identify horizontal asymptotes of rational functions.

concepts.name: Limit definition of derivative
concepts.summary: Compute f'(x) as the limit of (f(x+h)-f(x))/h for simple polynomial and rational functions.

concepts.name: Power and constant rules
concepts.summary: Differentiate polynomials and power functions term by term using the power, constant multiple and sum rules.

concepts.name: Product and quotient rules
concepts.summary: Apply the product and quotient rules correctly to differentiate products and ratios of functions.

concepts.name: Tangent line equations
concepts.summary: Write the equation of the tangent line at a point using the derivative as slope.

concepts.name: Differentiability and continuity
concepts.summary: Explain that differentiability implies continuity but not conversely, recognising corners, cusps and vertical tangents.

misconceptions.text: A 0/0 form means the limit does not exist.
The derivative of a product is the product of the derivatives.
A continuous function is always differentiable.

concepts.name: Chain rule
concepts.summary: Differentiate composite functions by multiplying the outer derivative evaluated at the inner function by the inner derivative.

concepts.name: Trigonometric derivatives
concepts.summary: Differentiate all six trig functions and combine them with product, quotient and chain rules.

concepts.name: Exponential and logarithmic derivatives
concepts.summary: Differentiate e^x, a^x, ln x and log_a x, including composite forms.

concepts.name: Implicit differentiation
concepts.summary: Differentiate relations in x and y by treating y as a function of x and solving for dy/dx.

concepts.name: Logarithmic differentiation
concepts.summary: Use logarithms to differentiate products, quotients and variable exponents like x^x.

concepts.name: Related rates
concepts.summary: Model a situation with a relation between changing quantities and differentiate in time to link their rates.

concepts.name: Higher-order derivatives
concepts.summary: Compute second and higher derivatives and interpret the second derivative as rate of change of slope.

misconceptions.text: In the chain rule you can skip the inner derivative, e.g. d/dx sin(3x) = cos(3x).
The derivative of a^x is x·a^(x-1), as with the power rule.
In related rates you should substitute the specific numerical values before differentiating with respect to time.

concepts.name: L'Hôpital's rule
concepts.summary: Decide when 0/0 or ∞/∞ forms permit differentiating numerator and denominator, and convert other indeterminate forms to those.

concepts.name: Intermediate Value Theorem
concepts.summary: Use continuity on a closed interval to justify the existence of roots and intermediate values.

concepts.name: Mean Value Theorem
concepts.summary: Verify hypotheses and use the theorem to guarantee a point where the tangent slope equals the average slope.

concepts.name: Critical points and first-derivative test
concepts.summary: Find critical points and use sign changes of f' to classify local maxima and minima.

concepts.name: Concavity and second-derivative test
concepts.summary: Use the sign of f'' to determine concavity, locate inflection points and classify critical points.

concepts.name: Absolute extrema on intervals
concepts.summary: Find global extrema on a closed interval by comparing critical-point and endpoint values.

concepts.name: Optimisation modelling
concepts.summary: Build an objective function with constraints, find the optimum, and justify that it is a maximum or minimum.

concepts.name: Curve sketching synthesis
concepts.summary: Combine domain, intercepts, asymptotes, monotonicity and concavity to sketch and justify a function's graph.

misconceptions.text: L'Hôpital's rule can be applied to any limit, and it means differentiating the quotient with the quotient rule.
Wherever f'(c)=0 there must be a local maximum or minimum.
Wherever f''(c)=0 there is an inflection point.

concepts.name: Formal epsilon-delta limits
concepts.summary: Construct and evaluate epsilon-delta arguments to prove limits and judge their correctness.

concepts.name: Proofs of differentiation rules
concepts.summary: Derive the product, quotient and chain rules from the limit definition and critique flawed proofs.

concepts.name: Consequences of the MVT
concepts.summary: Use the MVT to prove that functions with zero derivative are constant and that sign of f' determines monotonicity.

concepts.name: Linearisation and differentials
concepts.summary: Evaluate the accuracy of tangent-line approximations and propagate small errors using differentials.

concepts.name: Taylor polynomial approximation
concepts.summary: Construct Taylor polynomials and use the remainder to bound approximation error and to evaluate limits.

concepts.name: Pathological functions and counterexamples
concepts.summary: Assess how counterexamples show the limits of theorems, such as differentiable functions with discontinuous derivatives.

concepts.name: Inverse function differentiation
concepts.summary: Derive derivatives of inverse functions and inverse trig functions from the inverse derivative relation.

misconceptions.text: If f is differentiable, then f' must be continuous.
A Taylor series of a smooth function always converges to the function.
Tangent-line approximation error is the same size regardless of distance from the base point or curvature.
